title: Tequila and mezcal
lead: Agave spirits from Mexico: how tequila is aged, what makes mezcal smoky, and how guests order them.

sections.name: What tequila is

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Tequila is blue agave, from Mexico.

know: Blue Agave is the plant tequila is made from, in Mexico.
Piña the agave’s heart: cooked, crushed, fermented, distilled.
100% Agave says so on the label. If not, it’s a mixto.
Mixto needs only 51% of its sugar from agave.
sections.source: Mexican tequila standard NOM-006-SCFI (as summarized by Difford’s Guide)

sections.name: Blanco, reposado, añejo

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Tequila is sold by its time in oak.

know: Blanco is unaged or rested under two months: bright, peppery.
Reposado rests two months or more in oak: softer.
Añejo ages a year or more in oak: vanilla and caramel.
Cristalino is aged tequila filtered clear. Not a legal class.

read.bigIdea: Tequila is blue agave, from Mexico.
read.where: Tequila is made in **Mexico** from **blue Weber agave**. The heart of the plant, the **piña**, is cooked to turn its starch into sugar, then crushed, fermented and distilled. **100% de agave** tequila is made only from agave sugars. A bottle that just says “tequila” (a **mixto**) needs only **51%** of its sugars from agave.
read.mixup: **100% agave** says so on the label. If it doesn’t, it’s a **mixto**.
read.sayIt: It’s 100% agave, so it tastes bright and peppery.

keyPoints.line: is unaged or rested under two months: bright, peppery.
rests two months or more in oak: softer.
ages a year or more in oak: vanilla and caramel.
is aged tequila filtered clear. Not a legal class.

read.bigIdea: Tequila is sold by its time in oak.
read.where: **Blanco** is unaged or rested under two months: bright and **peppery**. **Reposado** rests in oak at least **two months**, so it’s softer. **Añejo** ages at least **a year**, picking up vanilla and caramel. **Extra añejo** ages at least **three years**. **Cristalino** is aged tequila **filtered clear**; it isn’t its own legal class.
read.visualIntro: Minimum time in oak, by law:
read.mixup: Clear doesn’t always mean young. A **cristalino** is aged, then filtered clear.
read.sayIt: The reposado is a little softer, with some oak. Great for sipping.

keyPoints.line: is where most mezcal is made.
can make mezcal. Espadín is the most common.
in the earth gives mezcal its smoke.

read.bigIdea: Mezcal is agave too, often smoky.
read.where: **Mezcal** is an agave spirit made mostly in **Oaxaca**, from **many kinds of agave**. **Espadín** is the most common; **tobalá** is a smaller, wild agave; an **ensamble** blends several. Roasting the agave in **earthen pits** gives mezcal its **smoky** taste. Tequila must be blue Weber agave; mezcal can use many agaves.
read.mixup: **Mezcal** isn’t a kind of tequila. It’s its own agave spirit, and the smoke comes from roasting.
read.sayIt: Would you like it smoky? Try it with mezcal.

keyPoints.line: reposado and añejo are often sipped slowly.
ask rocks or up, and salt or no salt.
if they name the bottle, ring in that one.

read.bigIdea: Blanco for citrus, aged for sipping.
read.where: Guests order tequila **in a Margarita**, **with a mixer** like soda or grapefruit soda, as a **shot**, or to **sip**. **Blanco** keeps citrus drinks bright; **reposado** and **añejo** suit sipping and stirred drinks. The classic Margarita in our book is served **on the rocks or up**, with a **salt rim**, so ask both. If they name the bottle, it’s a **call**.

stops.name: Margarita
stops.text: **Rocks or up**, salt or no salt.

stops.name: Tequila soda
stops.text: Blanco and **soda water** over ice, with lime.

stops.name: To sip
stops.text: Reposado or añejo, **neat** or **on the rocks**.

read.mixup: **Blanco** suits bright, citrus drinks. **Añejo** is softer and oakier, for sipping.
read.sayIt: Rocks or up? And salt on the rim?

keyPoints.line: is tequila, lime and orange liqueur.
is tequila, lime and grapefruit soda.
is mezcal, Aperol, yellow Chartreuse, lime.

read.where: The **Margarita** is tequila, lime and orange liqueur. The **Paloma** is tequila with lime and grapefruit soda. The **Tequila Sunrise** is tequila, orange juice and grenadine. The **Oaxaca Old Fashioned** uses reposado tequila **and** mezcal. The **Naked and Famous** is mezcal, Aperol, yellow Chartreuse and lime.
read.mixup: A **Margarita** is tequila, lime and orange liqueur. With Cognac and lemon instead, it’s a **Sidecar**.
read.sayIt: It’s built on tequila: bright, with a little pepper from the agave.

unverified: Tequila’s five DO states (Jalisco and parts of four others) are left out until checked against the CRT.
Mezcal categories are summarized from Wikipedia, not the 2016 standard itself.
Taste words (“soft”, “peppery”, “grassy”) are general bar descriptions, not from a rule. Bar lead to check them against our bottles.
How guests order (mixers, neat or on the rocks, shots) is common US bar usage, not a rule; bar lead to confirm the house wording.
